query_preparation.promotion_rule: Official map/API/register/download capability may be VERIFIED or PREPARED_QUERY, but exact candidate result remains pending until candidate-specific address/street/highway/provider/asset/record evidence and provenance are captured.

batches.c: OS Open UPRN supplies coordinates for UPRNs and is updated every six weeks. Nearest UPRN is not automatically the parcel address; exact addressable-location identity must be resolved.
A UPRN identifies an addressable location, not a legal title or parcel polygon. Parcel-to-UPRN association requires exact spatial/address evidence and may be one-to-many or none.

batches.t: OS Open USRN exact-street identifier preparation
batches.c: OS Open USRN is the authoritative street identifier dataset and is updated monthly. Exact candidate access street/USRN must be spatially bound before highway conclusions.
OS Open Roads provides a high-level connected road network updated every six months. Its centreline geometry is suitable for screening, not legal highway extent or access-right proof.
OS Open Names is updated quarterly and supports road/postcode/place lookup. Name or postcode agreement is a crosscheck only, not exact property identity.
UPRN, USRN, Open Roads and Open Names identifiers can be crosschecked, but inconsistencies must remain unresolved rather than silently reconciled.

batches.t: Street Manager live works exact-spatial query prep
batches.c: DfT Street Manager provides live England-wide utility street works and local highway authority road works. Exact candidate road/geometry and current permit status are required.
Works records carry status and traffic-management attributes; planned, in-progress, completed and cancelled states must not be merged.
GeoJSON activities and works data support construction-disruption screening. Traffic-management type and spatial extent must be retained for candidate use.
Forward plans are future coordination evidence, not current works. Candidate impact remains prospective until works/permit status becomes current.
Section 58 records can restrict subsequent street works after substantial road works. Exact street/extent/date and statutory exemptions must be resolved.
Potential clash/collaboration endpoints are coordination signals, not proof that the candidate itself is affected or that works will proceed.
DWI regulation guidance treats water supply zones as defined monitoring geographies. Exact candidate supplier and zone must be known before zone-level quality evidence is used.
DWI's July 2026 annual-report annex reports 2025 company testing volumes. Company totals are quality-system context, not candidate tap results.
Current DWI notices may be asset- or zone-specific. Exact supplier/zone/asset relationship and notice dates are required; unrelated company notices must not be generalized.
Treatment works, service reservoir and consumer-tap tests represent different points in the supply chain. They must not be treated as interchangeable parcel measurements.
Regulatory water-quality compliance does not establish pressure, flow, reinforcement need or development connection capacity.
Absence of a DWI notice for a candidate area is not proof of perfect quality or connection suitability; exact current zone evidence remains required.
Ofwat publishes GIS representations of water and sewerage undertaker areas. Exact point-in-boundary binding is required, and the legal appointment remains definitive.
New Appointments and Variations can replace the incumbent for specific areas. Candidate provider cannot be inferred solely from the surrounding incumbent company.
Water supply and sewerage undertakers can differ. Each service provider must be resolved independently before applying company-specific developer rules.
Ofwat describes requisition and self-lay routes for new mains/sewers. This is process context, not confirmation that a candidate connection is available.
Developer-services experience metrics are company-level incentives and cannot be converted into candidate-specific connection time, cost or probability.
Thames Water working-near-pipes guidance applies only where Thames is the relevant asset owner/provider. Exact provider and asset proximity must first be confirmed.

Thames Water states development is unlikely within five metres of its largest trunk mains or within three metres of distribution mains without diversion. Exact asset class and measured distance are required.
Thames Water states build-over agreements are required for building work within three metres of a public sewer or one metre of a public lateral drain. Exact sewer/lateral geometry is required.
Sewer diameter, asset type and proposal geometry affect the required route. A generic nearby-sewer indication is insufficient to classify an application.
Thames Water's 2026/27 new-connection charging arrangements took effect on 1 April 2026. Published schedules are not a site quote and scheme inputs remain required.
Public developer guidance and charges do not prove network capacity. Candidate capacity, reinforcement and quote remain pending provider assessment.
TfL open data includes the mapped boundary of roads for which TfL is highway authority. Exact candidate access/highway intersection is required; nearby TLRN is not parcel access.
TfL states LondonWorks provides current and planned roadworks, duration and promoter details. Planned works must remain separate from current disruption.
TfL's live traffic-disruption feed is refreshed on a five-minute cycle. Live disruption is transient operational context, not long-term site accessibility.
TfL publishes current Section 58/58A restrictions on its road network. Exact NSG/street extent and restriction dates are required before candidate construction implications.
Scaffolding, cranes, skips and other structures on TfL-managed roads require highway-licence handling. Applicability requires exact highway authority and construction interface.
Enfield maintains a register of adopted roads and offers written confirmation/plan searches. Road-list membership alone does not define the exact maintained highway boundary.
Enfield's current TMO page lists temporary, permanent and experimental orders. Exact road/extent/effective dates are required before applying a restriction to the sample.
Enfield issues temporary traffic orders for road works, events and other closures. Candidate impact requires exact street and active dates.
Enfield's lane-rental scheme became legally operational on 27 April 2026 and applies to 8.6% of borough roads. Exact candidate access road must be within the chargeable network/time.
Road adoption, TMO and lane-rental records are highway-management evidence, not proof of a legal vehicular access or approval for a new crossover.
Havering's live Highways Register identifies roads maintained at public expense and offers extent searches. Exact adopted extent requires the current plan/search, not a cached copy.
Havering directs users to confirmed roadworks on the current map and warns future unconfirmed works may lack detailed information. Confirmed and speculative works remain separate.
Havering CPZ and parking restrictions vary by street and time. Exact candidate street/bay/signage or map record is required; borough-level CPZ presence is insufficient.
Havering publishes Section 50, road-closure, scaffolding and crane licensing routes. Exact highway occupation and proposal type determine applicability and cost.
Parking bay suspensions require exact address, dates, bays and traffic-management details. They are construction logistics evidence, not development viability by themselves.

batches.t: Lambeth CPZ ArcGIS exact-polygon query gate
batches.c: Lambeth's official CPZ Feature Layer supports JSON/GeoJSON query and contains zone/hours fields. Exact point-in-polygon response is required for the Lambeth candidate.
Lambeth TMOs are the statutory legal basis for traffic and parking restrictions. Exact made/order status, road extent and operative date are required.
Lambeth's weekly streetworks update lists major current works with references, locations, traffic impact and dates. Exact candidate-road relation is required.
Streetworks may be undertaken by utilities or the council. Promoter, works reference and traffic impact must be preserved rather than inferred from location alone.
Temporary traffic restrictions and road closures are date-specific. Historic or future notices cannot be treated as current candidate access restrictions.
CPZ geometry, TMO legal records and weekly streetworks must agree on street identity/time before any candidate construction-access conclusion is promoted.
